Before you begin / Set up your workspace

Four tools. One folder. Start simple.

1. Writing: open ChatGPT or Claude for scripts.
2. Images: choose a generator that accepts a character reference.
3. Video: open Canva or CapCut to assemble your reel.
4. Tracking: open Google Sheets or Excel for your results.

Create a folder named “AI Creator.”
Inside it, make: 01 Character, 02 Images, 03 Videos, and 04 Results.
Start with one social platform. Choose tools you can access; check their costs and commercial-use terms.

Done when: your folder exists and you can open each tool.

Your first win: write one useful promise, draft one reel, and finish the launch checklist. Start there.

02 / Identity

A familiar face.
A recognizable point of view.

Done when: you have a character brief, one reference image, and three matching scenes.

01

Write the character brief

Copy the prompt below into your AI assistant. Fill in the brackets. Save the answer as “My character brief.”

02

Approve one reference

Use an image tool with character-reference support. Generate a fictional adult. Pick one image and save it as your master reference.

03

Render, compare, approve

Attach the master reference to each new image request. Make three separate scenes. Compare the face, hair and distinctive features.

Open the copy-ready character prompt

Create a character brief for a fictional adult AI creator who helps [audience] with [problem]. Give me: a name, a one-line bio that says AI-generated, three personality traits, three weekly content topics, and a consistent visual description. Use [colors and style]. Do not copy a real person or invent personal product experiences.

Copy the image prompt for your next scene

Use the attached fictional character reference. Keep the same facial features, hair and distinctive marks. Create one vertical scene of the character [action] in [setting]. Use [lighting and colors]. Leave space for a short text overlay. Do not add text, watermarks or extra panels.

Quality gate: reject blurred upscales, contact-sheet grid lines, changing facial features, watermarks, and awkward crops. Keep rejected images as briefs for a new render.

04 / Hook studio

Earn the pause.
Deliver the payoff.

A hook is the first line of your post. It tells someone why they should keep watching.

Build your next opening line

Test one angle at a time

Only promise a payoff your video actually delivers. Use proof you can show; skip invented results.

A reel you can build todayExample / travel
Hook
“3 weekend escapes.
Which one fits your budget?”

Show three real destinations. Compare a useful cost or planning detail for each. Explain what changes the price.

Payoff: a clear comparison viewers can use.
Next step: “Get the weekend planner through the link in my bio.”

Verify prices and locations. Label generated scenes. Use a comment keyword only when its delivery flow is working.

01 / OPENSay the promise

First 1–2 seconds: a specific question or useful result.

02 / SHOWMake the steps visible

One idea per shot. Number the items. Cut the filler.

03 / RESOLVEClose the loop

Deliver the answer you promised. Make it worth saving.

04 / INVITEOffer one next step

Save, follow, or get the checklist. Pick one main action.

Make the reel: follow these exact steps
  1. Open Canva or CapCut. Create a vertical 1080 × 1920 video.
  2. Import three approved images. Put them in order on the timeline.
  3. Add your hook as text on the first scene. Start with about two seconds.
  4. Add one useful tip to each scene. Allow enough time to read it.
  5. Add a final card: “Get the free [checklist] through the link in my bio.”
  6. Use your own voice or licensed audio. Keep text away from the screen edges.
  7. Export an MP4. Watch it on your phone. Fix tiny text, awkward cuts or wrong facts.
  8. Upload to your chosen platform. Add required AI and commercial labels. Publish and record the post link.

Done when: your first video is live and your checklist link works.

05 / The offer

Give attention
somewhere useful to go.

An offer is something people can buy. Start with one small resource that solves the problem you post about.

Useful postEarn interest
→
Free resourceDeliver a small win
→
Email opt-inAsk permission
→
Relevant offerSolve the next problem

Start with one small offer.

Travel ideas → weekend itinerary template.
Style guides → capsule wardrobe planner.
Creator education → content planning workbook.

Keep the free resource useful on its own. Explain what the paid resource adds. Disclose affiliate relationships.

Copy a clear call to action

Your next step is already mapped out. Get the [resource] to turn [problem] into [specific next action]. See exactly what’s included before you choose.

Build the free-resource link: step by step
  1. Open Canva or a document editor. Make a one-page checklist that matches your video.
  2. Export it as a PDF. Test that every link opens.
  3. In an email service such as MailerLite, create a signup form. Say what people receive and whether they are joining your emails. Include your privacy notice.
  4. Add the PDF link to the welcome email or signup thank-you page.
  5. Publish the signup page. Put its URL in your profile’s link field, if available.
  6. Test with your own email. Confirm the signup and open the delivered PDF.

Done when: someone can go from your profile to the delivered checklist. Exact menu names vary by service.

Later: test brand work, licensing or platform monetization when your account qualifies. Confirm current eligibility in the app.

06 / The 90-day experiment

Grow what works.
Change what doesn’t.

Use these milestones to guide experiments. They are planning targets, not platform rules or promised results.

Days 01–30

Find a repeatable series

  • Pin your promise, best example and next step.
  • Test three recurring formats.
  • Compare retention and shares with your own median.
Review at day 14If ten posts show weak openings, change the hook and first shot.
Days 31–60

Build a reason to return

  • Repeat the format that gets the best response.
  • Number episodes and tease the next useful topic.
  • Offer a free checklist in exchange for an email, with clear signup consent.
Review at day 45Views without follows? Clarify the series promise. Few opt-ins? Improve the resource and invitation.
Days 61–90

Test willingness to pay

  • Release one focused offer.
  • Make a one-page brand sheet: audience, example posts, actual views and contact details.
  • Pitch ten relevant brands with specific ideas.
Review at day 90No sales? Talk with ten potential buyers about the problem, offer and price before expanding.
Your weekly routine: open post analytics. Record views, average watch time, shares, new followers, email signups and sales. Pick your strongest post. Make a new version with one change.
Download the research and weekly review worksheets

CSV files open in Excel, Google Sheets, or Numbers. Add your own observations; these templates contain no invented results.
